items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Bubber Bubba Miley in the context of Duke Ellington's early work; Interviewee does not respond with personal connection.

ctx.x: And quite often, the solos are the things that we would think, if we only heard one version, would think were improvised. Indeed, we're not. I mean, they're very, very close to each other. This happens on a number of early Duke Ellington things, even indeed, with Bubber Bubba Miley and so forth -- the famous case of the Dipper Mouth solo, which was a set solo.

So I was just wondering -- I don't want to make a great deal out of just those few examples, but if there really was that much improvising, if improvising was ... I don't know quite how to put it ... as much a part of the jazzman's trade back then as it was now, what -- now, I think we assume that most people that we call 'jazzmen' are very, very capable improvisers. Was that the case then?
